pennies or dimes destroy these pumps quickly but the good news is that minimal tools are needed if you have the skill to open the washer wrapper properly.
Remove two console screws without loosing them as they are very specially prepared for that job.
Unplug the spin lockout electric plug
Mark the orientation and remove the two big green spring clips.
Rotate the wrapper forward while noting how it keys into the base by looking past the lid hole. This is important as it is first time tricky.
Back the wrapper away to reveal the pump
Using long nose locking plier tool move hose clamps back and unplug hoses.
Study how the pump mount clips tag into the motor as this is not immediately clear the first time you do this.
Unclip the two clips and note they will fall away easily.
Pull the old pump off while noting that there are two plastic locating pins that must be in place when you plug in the new pump.
Note the orientation of the flats of the motor drive and align the new pump to match
Re-assemble the machine.

It SAVED yet another case of "someone" leaving change in their pockets. removed pump (10 minutes), cleared the coin from the screen, and reinstalled. Impeller blades were saved!! hurray!
So instead of clogging the pump itself and damaging the impellers, and then buying a fourth pump, it just clogged my screen, I just cleared the clog in 5 seconds.
If the washer manufacturers would just put this screen into their designs, it would save millions of hours of wasted time and money for us owners.

Original Review-
A failed pump is one of the most common problems with almost any washing machine. In my case, I am still teaching my wife that COINS cannot go into the washer. this is the 3rd pump in 8 years. but having coins in the pump will simply chew up the pump vanes or worse, burn up the motor. This took only about 20min to install. and most of this time was just spent trying to minimize the water spilling from the hose and avoiding a mess. Just use the control diagnostics (read the manual) and you can confirm if your pump is dead. Repair guy was going to charge me $150 to "look at the washer." and for sure another $200+ to repair it.
IF they would sell just the pump vanes, I would buy 6 of them to keep on the shelf. Too bad they do not incorporate a course screen in the inlet.
